Definition: Brief, repeated exchanges between gardeners and passers-by across the garden boundary.
Include when: The garden starts the conversation: produce, weather, what is growing.
Exclude when: Organised events such as harvest suppers (note them in the memo instead).
Example: I don't garden, but I know everyone's tomatoes by now.

Definition: A sense that the garden puts friendly eyes on the street.
Include when: Safety, being noticed, people looking out for each other or for property.
Exclude when: Complaints about the garden itself (use Gatekeeping or Change).
Example: Someone's always there till dark. I walk that way home now.

Definition: The garden as a place to calm down, recover or be alone.
Include when: Stress, mood, quiet, time out from work or caring.
Exclude when: Exercise talked about as fitness (use Active body).
Example: It's the only hour of the week nobody needs anything from me.

Definition: Physical activity that comes from gardening or getting to the garden.
Include when: Digging, carrying, walking there, feeling fitter.
Example: My knees complain, but I'm moving more than I have in years.

Definition: Produce given away, swapped or cooked together.
Include when: Any exchange of food, including with non-gardeners.
Example: We leave the extra courgettes on the wall with a sign.

Definition: Waiting lists, plot allocation, tenure rules.
Include when: Formal routes in and the time they take.
Example: Four years on the list. I've stopped asking.

Definition: Informal rules, cliques or norms that make people feel unwelcome.
Include when: Feeling watched, judged or not part of the in-group.
Example: There's a way you're supposed to do things, and nobody tells you what it is.

Definition: Worry that the garden or wider improvements push up rents or change who lives in the area.
Include when: Rent, house prices, new residents, being priced out.
Exclude when: General change with no cost element.
Example: It's lovely. It's also on the estate agent's leaflet now.
